mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen monotonically each of the last three weeks (-16.1 to -12.1), indicating a steady recovery trend in discretionary mobility that should continue for the next four weeks absent a shock.
evidence_refs: fact: RETAIL_REC increased from -16.1 to -12.1 over 4 weeks
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not higher than the last 28 days despite the prior monotonic uptrend persisting through the snapshot.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility jumped sharply in the most recent week (-14.7 to -10.7), suggesting a surge in outdoor leisure activity that typically spills over into nearby retail and recreation visits within one to two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises more than 3 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact: PARKS rose 4.0 points from t-1w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise within two weeks of a PARKS jump exceeding 3 points, or declines instead.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT remains deeply suppressed (around -20) while WORKPLACES only partially recovered, indicating continued restrictions or caution on commuting infrastructure; if TRANSIT drops further below -22, it signals renewed tightening that will suppress RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact: TRANSIT sits near -20 to -22 across all four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days even though TRANSIT falls below -22, invalidating the suppression linkage.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has stayed flat and elevated (~11.3-11.9) for four weeks, indicating a stable behavioral equilibrium where people remain home-based; this stability implies RETAIL_REC growth will plateau rather than continue rising sharply.
evidence_refs: fact: RESIDENTIAL stayed within 11.3-11.9 range for 4 weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to rise substantially (>2 points) over the next 28 days despite RESIDENTIAL staying flat, contradicting the plateau prediction.

mechanism_narrative: The joint recovery of WORKPLACES and TRANSIT together drives RETAIL_REC because commuting trips generate incidental retail stops; only when both rise together does the combined effect exceed the threshold needed to meaningfully lift retail footfall over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT increase week-on-week simultaneously
evidence_refs: fact: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both show partial recovery from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise even when WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both increase in the same week, or rises when only one increases.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has turned positive and stable (0.1 to 3.6), suggesting essential-trip normalization; combined with rising PARKS, this signals broader willingness to leave home which should interact to amplify RETAIL_REC gains beyond what either series alone would predict.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM positive and PARKS rising simultaneously
evidence_refs: fact: GROCERY_PHARM rose from 0.1 to 3.6 while PARKS rose from -15.0 to -10.7
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise within two weeks when both GROCERY_PHARM is positive and PARKS is rising concurrently.

mechanism_narrative: The pronounced jump in PARKS (-14.7 to -10.7) in the final week aligns with a seasonal transition toward warmer-weather outdoor activity, which historically precedes a broader seasonal uplift in retail and recreation visits within a four-week window.
evidence_refs: fact: PARKS increased by 4.0 points in the most recent week, the largest single-week jump in the snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to trend upward over the next four weeks despite the seasonal PARKS uplift persisting or growing further.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES mobility reverses and drops sharply week-on-week (a signal of renewed workplace closures or restrictions), this policy-driven contraction will spill over to suppress retail and recreation visits within one week due to reduced daytime population circulation.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls more than 5 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact: WORKPLACES has fluctuated between -8.3 and -10.7 over the last four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall within one week following a WORKPLACES drop exceeding 5 points week-on-week.
